In the future it seems likely that urban densities and oil prices may increase to a degree that our current patterns in transit usage my be forced to change. There are also new tech advances (Driverless cars) which could alter our morning commutes drastically.

What are your favorite advances in transit? How do you see the transit infrastructure operating in a big city like Los Angeles or London in 25 years? 50 years?

Obviously it's difficult to predict future developments in any field but I think it's fun to wonder and dream about! So what's your vision for the future?
Transit development in the near future

This a great topic. I think it's pretty clear that the driver-less car is going to change everything. As soon as it hits the popular consciousness that accidents will nearly vanish there will be no stopping it. Roads and highways will be completely redesigned to remove elements that exist for human drivers that machines don't use or need. Los Angeles, New York, and London will be completely different cities form the advent of driver-less cars alone.

Americans are just now starting to figure out their infrastructure is aged and garbage. There is lot of optimism that they'll repair/replace it with some really innovative stuff.

My theory is that we're entering the era of micro transit. Rather than transit systems built around moving large numbers of people or a large mass of goods, future transportation (by land) will be more focused on point to point transportation of individual people and packages. I'm envisioning very small autonomous "taxis" (1 or 2 seats) for most people-moving in cities, and small autonomous vehicles for delivering packages. Buses will probably disappear, and cities that don't already have extensive train systems will find that they don't need to build them (in much the same way that cities in developing nations don't need to build land-line telecom networks).
